observation: Three node reports (rf, ltu, dump) for event slac-001 all assess the data as suspicious. The ltu report identifies a sustained, high-significance position excursion at BPMS:LTUH:250:X (peak robust z ≈ 62.5, 42 consecutive samples) with a concurrent sustained charge disturbance at BPMS:LTUH:450:TMIT (peak robust z ≈ 78.7, 301 low-charge samples), while the position excursion at BPMS:LTUH:450:X coincides with low-charge masking and is likely a sentinel artifact. The dump report shows coincident, sustained low-charge disturbances at BPMS:DMPH:502:TMIT and BPMS:DMPH:693:TMIT (~300 consecutive samples, shared onset), with position excursions consistent with masked low-charge sentinel behavior. The rf report shows a ~99.96% peak RF amplitude deviation from a 69.12 baseline with only 20 valid updates across 725 samples (705 NaN, i.e., no new update). Onset timestamps from all three instruments fall within the candidate window, with pairwise differences of ~2.5 s (rf later than ltu/dump) and ~8 ms between ltu and dump. No RF phase data or protein data are available. Only aggregate node reports are available; unique RF cause cannot be established from these summaries.

The LTUH:450:X excursion coincides with low-charge masking (~300 samples) and is consistent with a sentinel artifact. No RF phase data are available. Onsets for all instruments fall within the candidate window, but the RF onset trails the beam onsets by approximately 2.5 seconds.
